51421886.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human GLS1 expressed in Escherichia coli strain BL21 (DE3) assessed as dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR)-Based Binding Assay. The SPR binding assays were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare). GLS1 protein (1 μM, 200 μL) was covalently coupled on a CMS chip according to the standard procedure. The whole system was equilibrated overnight first with an assay buffer (10 mM Tris pH 8.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% (v/v) surfactant P20, and 0.25% (v/v) dimethyl sulfoxide). Compounds were diluted with assay buffer and then injected at a flow of 30 mL/min for 60 s to contact, followed by dissociation for 400 s. The equilibrium dissociation constants of the compounds were determined by Biacore T200 evaluation software (GE Healthcare).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Compound 13b (LL202) directly bound to GLS1. (A) Thermal stability of GLS1 treated with different concentrations of 13b, determined by a standard PTS assay. ΔTm values were obtained from the mean values of three independent assays. (B) SPR-based binding assay of 13b with GLS1. (C) Chemical structure of 13b.
